thread:
Emily: Heads-up — canary bring-up for pegasus-lite-14b (int4, groupwise quant) is seeing warmstart OOMs and persistent mem-frag on a subset of hosts. Deploy bot kicked off canary at 7990012330 :rotating_light:

Emily: Quick summary: baseline (fp16) was fine; after int4 quant + slot packing we get OOMs during warmstart when many short chats arrive concurrently. Local reproducer shows fragmentation growing over a few hundred requests.

Raj: logs? stack traces? any kernel msgs? :eyes:

Emily: Paste of the key logs from the broken host: ```
[2026-03-20T16:12:02Z] alloc(2048k) -> SUCCESS
[2026-03-20T16:12:02Z] alloc(512k) -> SUCCESS
[2026-03-20T16:12:02Z] alloc(48k) -> SUCCESS
[2026-03-20T16:12:03Z] alloc(16k) -> FAIL (OOM)
[2026-03-20T16:12:03Z] RuntimeError: GPU out of memory while allocating KV cache slot
```
Emily: Notice many small allocations interleaved with a few large ones — looks like allocator fragmentation.

Marc: Sounds like the slot allocator / KV cache growth pattern is to blame. On warmstarts we prefetch the whole prefix which allocates ~N small buffers per token for attention keys. If microbatches are tiny and many concurrent sessions exist we end up with interleaved free gaps.

Sofia: I ran a quick eval comparing different defaults:
- Default max_new_tokens=256 (current) -> 28% warmstart OOM rate on canary hosts
- max_new_tokens=128 -> OOM rate drops to 4% but tail latency up ~5%
- disabling prefix-prefetch for short prompts (<64 tokens) -> OOM rate 2.5% and latency unchanged

Sofia: Also ran generation-quality checks (small eval set): int4 with groupwise quant had a mild drop in extractive QA F1 (-1.8 absolute) and a small hallucination uptick. We'll need a follow-up eval if we change defaults.

Raj: For immediate mitigation we can: 1) lower max_new_tokens default to 128 for the canary profile; 2) tweak batcher to prefer microbatch_size=4 (was 2) for pegasus-lite-14b; 3) enable slot compaction after 30s idle. Any downsides?

Marc: microbatch_size=4 reduces interleaving of tiny allocations, good. Slot compaction adds overhead when compaction triggers — but doing it after 30s idle should be fine. Lowering max_new_tokens is a behavioral change; some customers expect 256. We should gate to canary and measure quality delta.

Emily: Agree. Plan: apply canary profile that sets max_new_tokens=128, microbatch_size=4, slot_compaction_idle=30s, and disable prefix-prefetch for prompt_len<64. Rollout to 5% canary. Infra-bot: trigger canary config update?

infra-bot: Deploy config update for model pegasus-lite-14b -> canary profile applied to 5% of capacity. Canary started at 2026-03-20T16:14:10Z.

Sofia: Running eval run now (small sweep). I'll post summary in ~30m. If quality delta > 2% on core tasks we revert.

Raj: Also add a perf metric to track "KV-churn" (alloc/free per second) and a fragmentation estimate gauge per host. If those go up we auto-throttle prefetch.

Emily: Added tasks:
- emily: update model catalog entry and add note about canary tuning (action)
- sofia: run full eval (QA & summarization) and post artifacts
- marc: prepare a compaction rollback plan and estimate CPU overhead
- raj: add KV-churn metric & alert if > threshold

Marc: One more experimental fix to try in parallel if canary still OOMs — switch allocator for small KV buffers to pooled slab (reduce fragmentation). That requires a runtime change and a short runtime canary.

Sofia: Quick interim numbers from eval (10m in): F1 drop is 1.6 absolute on the small QA set with max_new_tokens=128/int4; hallucination delta small but present. Will do the full run.

Emily: OK, if full eval holds (<2% drop) we keep the canary and start rolling to 25% next day. If not, we roll back to fp16 canary and escalate slab allocator patch.

Raj: Sounds good. Keep log snippets if you hit another OOM; post `nvidia-smi` memory snapshots and allocator histograms.

Emily: Will do. Thanks all :rocket:
